answers.question: Tell me about yourself. Take about 90 seconds and focus on why you fit the AI Computer Vision Engineer role.
answers.text: Hi, I'm Avery Morgan. I'm studying an Advanced Diploma of Information Technology in Artificial Intelligence at Harbour Technical College, with hands-on coursework in object detection, video analytics and dataset quality. In 2025 I worked as a Computer Vision Lab Assistant in the college's Applied Computing Lab. I prepared and checked annotated training images, reproduced baseline experiments, logged metrics and documented setup steps, and I helped classmates debug their data-loading and evaluation scripts. My strongest project is Smart Intersection Object Detection. I curated and labelled a small image dataset, trained a lightweight YOLO model, and compared precision, recall and mAP across experiments. I then reviewed false positives and missed detections, and documented the limitations caused by low light, occlusion and the small training set. I presented it as a finalist at the Harbour Applied AI Showcase. I also built a warehouse safety prototype that highlights people entering marked safety zones in recorded video, with object tracking, event counts and latency measured on a laptop. I fit the AI Computer Vision Engineer role because it asks for Python, OpenCV and a deep-learning framework like PyTorch, which are the tools I use in every project, and because I care about evaluating models carefully, not just training them.

answers.question: Give a 2-minute introduction: your background, one highlight project, and why you want the AI Computer Vision Engineer role.
answers.text: Hi, I'm Avery Morgan, and thank you for having me. I'm an Artificial Intelligence diploma student at Harbour Technical College, finishing in November 2026. Before that, I completed a Certificate Four in Information Technology, in programming, at City Skills Institute. In 2025 I worked as a Computer Vision Lab Assistant, where I checked annotated training images, reproduced baseline experiments and helped classmates debug their evaluation scripts. Earlier, as a Customer Technology Assistant at Harbour Electronics, I explained product features and resolved setup issues, which taught me to explain technical things clearly. The project I'm proudest of is Smart Intersection Object Detection. I built a prototype that detects vehicles, cyclists and pedestrians in recorded intersection footage. I curated and labelled a small image dataset, trained a lightweight YOLO model with PyTorch, and compared precision, recall and mAP across experiments. The most important part was the error analysis. I reviewed false positives and missed detections, and documented the limitations caused by low light, occlusion and the deliberately small training set. It is an offline demonstration, not a deployed traffic system, and I presented it as a finalist at the Harbour Applied AI Showcase in 2025. I also created a Dataset Quality Review Toolkit, a small FastAPI service with SQL storage, automated tests and Docker packaging, which checks images and annotations before training. I want the AI Computer Vision Engineer role because it brings together the work I enjoy most: training detection models, working with video, and evaluating results carefully. I'm still building experience with large datasets and video pipelines, and this role is where I want to grow that.
